catalog_quote: [Riedel & Patin 2011, p. 144 fn. 3:] All Fipa varieties are fully tonal. Milanzi, Nkansi and Kwa have 7 vowels: [a] [E] [i] [I] [O] [u] [U] (Lungu and Mambwe only have [a] [E] [i] [O] [u]). Vowel length is contrastive, but there is also syntactically conditioned penultimate lengthening. The tonal analysis of Fipa is incomplete, because of this we do not mark tone in the sections dealing with morphosyntax. ... [p. 153, 3.1:] The question, in Fipa, is generally expressed by a boundary H(L)% tone. The tone appears on the last syllable of the Intonational Phrase (see below), which is then lengthened ... [p. 155:] When there is a lexical high on the penult, the boundary H(L)% is maintained, but is downstepped ... audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote check: every quoted passage (Riedel & Patin 2011 fn. 3 p. 144, sec. 3.1 p. 153, p. 155; Struck 1911 p. 962 6d, 9c, Quellen p. 953) is verbatim in the copies we hold at the stated line ranges. Deciding source: a 2011 open-access fieldwork article with instrumental pitch data on three Fipa varieties by Bantuists (Riedel later co-authored the only Fipa tone study); it states Fipa is fully tonal with contrastive vowel length and syntactically conditioned penultimate lengthening and never posits word stress, which matches the tonal coding with phrase-domain penult lengthening; Struck 1911's hedged penult 'dynamischer Ton' from c. 50 second-hand words is correctly kept as the historical claim. PHOIBLE 1659 (from Riedel & Bickmore 2013) independently lists a H tone segment and length pairs, consistent. Glottolog 5.1 (42 [fip] entries read locally) and a Crossref search show no reference gramma
